source.snippet: HN commenter: 'When we rented our house the garage door opener was broken. The landlord sent a guy who was completely incompetent... I knew that a new one would come with this MyQ scam and also not work with Homelink (car integration) which would be a huge downgrade. So I fixed it myself rather than get a free new one. Someone should start a business ripping this crap out of garage door openers and replacing it with something that works locally and doesn't require a subscription.'

problem_statement: Homeowners and landlords are forced into cloud-dependent, subscription-based garage door opener ecosystems (e.g. MyQ) that break car Homelink integration and require ongoing fees, with no straightforward local-control replacement service available.
target_segment: Homeowners, landlords, and property managers who own or manage smart garage door openers and want local/offline control without vendor lock-in or subscriptions.
notes: Explicit 'someone should start a business' call-out from an HN commenter. Buyer willing-to-pay evidence: user declined a free new opener specifically to avoid the MyQ ecosystem cost and lock-in — implying they'd pay for a quality local-control retrofit. Landlords and property managers with multiple units represent a recurring revenue angle (installation + support per unit). Signal is a single comment; needs validation across more sources before high confidence.
